props.gloss_en: whoever says David sinned is nothing but mistaken
as it is said: 'and David was successful in all his ways, and the Lord was with him' (I Sam 18:14) -- is it possible that sin came to his hand and the Shechina was with him?
how then do I uphold 'why have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil'? -- that he sought to do and did not do
Rav: Rebbi, who comes from David, turns about and expounds in David's merit
Rebbi: this evil differs from all the evils in the Torah, for of all the evils in the Torah 'and he did' is written, and here 'to do' is written
'Uriah the Hittite you struck with the sword' -- that you should have judged him in the Sanhedrin and did not judge
'and his wife you took to yourself as a wife' -- you have taking in her
whoever goes out to the war of the house of David writes a bill of severance for his wife
as it is said: 'and these ten cheeses bring to the captain of the thousand, and visit your brothers for peace, and take their arubatam' (I Sam 17:18)
what is arubatam? Rav Yosef taught: matters that are shared between him and her
'and him you killed with the sword of the children of Ammon' -- as for the sword of the children of Ammon you are not punished, so for Uriah the Hittite you are not punished
what is the reason? he was a rebel against the kingship
for he said to him: 'and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open field' (II Sam 11:11)
Rav: when you examine David, you find nothing in him except [the matter] of Uriah
as it is written: 'save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite' (I Kings 15:5)
David accepted slander

as it is written: '...Ziba said to the king: behold, he is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-Devar' (II Sam 9:4), and it is written: '...and took him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-Devar' (9:5)

since he saw he was a liar, when he slandered him again why did he accept it from him? as it is written '...behold, he is staying in Jerusalem' (II Sam 16:3); and from where do we know he accepted it? as it is written 'and the king said: behold, all that is Mefiboshet's is yours' (16:4)
Shmuel: he saw evident things in him

as it is written: 'and Mefiboshet son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had not dressed his feet nor trimmed his moustache nor washed his clothes...' (II Sam 19:25), and it is written: 'and when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king...' (19:26-28, 30-31)
he said to him: I said 'when will you come in peace', and you do this to me? Not against you do I have grievances but against Him who brought you in peace
this is what is written: 'and the son of Jonathan was Meriv-Baal' (I Chr 8:34) -- was Meriv-Baal his name? was not Mefiboshet his name? rather, because he made a quarrel with his Master
a bat kol went out and said to him: quarreller son of a quarreller
'quarreller' -- what we said; 'son of a quarreller' -- as it is written: 'and Saul came to the city of Amalek and quarrelled in the valley' (I Sam 15:5)
R' Mani: over the matter of the valley
when David said to Mefiboshet 'you and Ziba shall divide the field', a bat kol went out and said to him: Rehoboam and Jeroboam shall divide the kingdom
had David not accepted slander, the kingdom of the house of David would not have been divided
...and Israel would not have worshipped idols
...and we would not have been exiled from our land
